jobs.description:
Job Overview:
The HR Manager will serve as a strategic business partner and trusted advisor to leaders across the Coffee Business Unit's corporate functions, providing HR expertise and leadership to support the execution of business priorities, organizational effectiveness, and talent strategies.
This role will partner closely with Vice Presidents, Directors, and functional leadership teams across key Coffee Business Unit corporate functions, including Finance, Commercial Strategy , Digital & Technology, Human Resources, and other shared services organizations. The HR Business Partner will play a critical role in helping leaders build organizational capability, develop talent, drive engagement, and enable business performance through thoughtful people strategies and practical HR solutions.
The successful candidate will possess strong business acumen, executive presence, and the ability to influence across a matrixed organization. This individual will balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution and be comfortable navigating organizational change, leadership transitions, workforce planning, talent discussions, and complex employee relations matters in a fast-paced environment.
Key Responsibilities
- Serve as the primary HR business partner to leaders within assigned Coffee Business Unit corporate functions, ensuring people strategies align with business objectives and organizational priorities.

- Partner with functional leadership teams to assess organizational effectiveness, workforce capabilities, talent needs, and succession plans to support current and future business growth.

- Provide strategic coaching and consultation to Vice Presidents, Directors, and people leaders on organizational design, talent management, performance, employee engagement, and leadership effectiveness.

- Partner with business leaders to identify capability gaps and develop talent strategies that strengthen organizational performance and leadership pipelines.

- Support organizational changes, business transformation initiatives, restructuring activities, leadership transitions, and other strategic projects impacting Coffee corporate functions.

- Leverage workforce analytics, engagement data, talent metrics, and business insights to identify trends and deliver recommendations that inform leadership decision-making.

- Facilitate talent reviews, succession planning, leadership assessments, and development planning across supported functions.

- Collaborate with HR Centers of Excellence to deliver integrated talent solutions, including recruiting, onboarding, compensation, learning and development, and performance management.

- Drive the successful implementation of enterprise HR programs while ensuring alignment with the unique needs of Coffee Business Unit corporate teams.

- Provide guidance and support related to employee relations matters, workplace concerns, policy interpretation, and performance issues while ensuring consistency and compliance.

- Support annual HR processes including performance management, talent planning, compensation cycles, engagement action planning, and organizational reviews.

- Develop executive-ready presentations, analyses, and recommendations related to talent, organization effectiveness, workforce planning, and employee engagement.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Associate Brand Manager - MBA (Burlington, MA)
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Summer 2027 MBA Marketing Intern ship
Associate Brand Manager · Burlington, MA
10-Week Summer Program · June 7 – August 13, 2027
Full-Time / Hybrid

Build a career with flavor at Keurig Dr Pepper! Our MBA Marketing Internship gives first-year business school students the chance to tackle real brand challenges, develop best-in-class marketing skills, and leave a lasting mark on one of our iconic brands. Each intern is assigned an individual stretch project , spanning from brand strategy and consumer insights to data analysis and go-to-market planning , with final recommendations presented to our senior marketing leaders.

ABOUT THE PROGRAM
Our comprehensive internship experience is built on four pillars of support:
COACHING & FEEDBACK
- Consistent mentorship and feedback throughout the program

- Coaching & support from former interns

- Mid-point & final performance evaluations

HOLISTIC MARKETING TRAINING
- Marketing fundamentals

- Analytics & financials

- Consumer insights

- Operations & route-to-market

- Leadership & influencing skills

CULTURE & NETWORKING EVENTS
- Formal networking events with Marketing leaders

- ABM roundtable & feedback discussions

- Leadership coffee chats & happy hours

ACCESS TO LEADERSHIP
- Executive meet & greets

- Formal & informal leadership exposure

- Opportunities to build personal connections across the organization

WHAT YOU'LL DO
As an intern, you will be assigned a project designed to stretch your analytical and strategic thinking . Throughout the summer you will develop and strengthen key managerial competencies with support from a dedicated Project Lead and Mentor .

TRANSFORM DATA TO INSIGHTS
Dive into brand, industry, and consumer data to  identify  business issues and opportunities. L earn how to use multiple data sources ( i ncluding tools such as  IRI, Numerator , and YouGov) t o uncover actionable insights and develop evidence-backed strategic recommendations ; and t hrive with support from your Data Buddy , a dedicated resource for you throughout the program .

GENERATE FUEL FOR GROWTH
Own and drive your individual summer brand project end-to-end, from  initial  scoping through final presentation to senior leaders. Work collaboratively with your Project Lead and cross-functional partners to shape your approach, build your story, and develop a fully formed strategic recommendation. Projects span areas such as brand strategy, innovation, digital shelf, consumer insights, and go-to-market planning.

CHAMPION CONSUMER OBSESSED BRAND BUILDING
Develop your understanding of the consumer : who they are, what they need, and how our brands can serve them better. Translate consumer insights into clear, actionable implications that inform your brand project recommendations. Begin building a working knowledge of brand equity fundamentals and what sets our brands apart in the marketplace.

SHAPE BRAND STRATEGY
Contribute to brand planning conversations and  assist  in developing materials that bring your recommendations to life. Gain exposure to annual brand planning, budgeting processes, st rategic frameworks and cross-functional brand alignment under the guidance of your Project Lead.

AMPLIFY IMPACT WITH CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION
Engage with colleagues across Marketing, Consumer Insights, Finance, Innovation, Sales, and Operations to gather input and build a well-rounded business perspective. We challenge each intern to schedule at least five coffee chats with marketers outside of their day-to-day team over the course of the summer.

PRESENT TO MARKETING LEADERSHIP
Deliver a 25–30-minute strategic presentation to senior Marketing leadership covering your key insights, strategic approaches, recommendations, and implementation considerations. Q&A follows. This is your moment to  showcase  your thinking and the impact of your work.

Total Rewards:
- $2,250/week

- Paid bi-weekly

- $7,000 sign-on bonus, paid within first 30 days of employment

Requirements:
- Currently enrolled in a two-year, full-time MBA program; must be between your 1st and 2nd year (expected graduation the year following the internship)

- 3–6 years of full-time, post-undergraduate professional experience

- Strong analytical aptitude — able to work with data and translate findings into stories and strategic action

- Proficiency  in Excel and PowerPoint

- Ability to manage multiple priorities in a cross-functional, fast-paced environment

- Marketing concentration is not  required  but is a plus

- CPG, beverage, or brand marketing experience is a plus

- Experience with syndicated marketing research databases (e.g.,  Circana /IRI, Numerator, YouGov, Mintel) is a plu s

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
Our ideal intern brings a general manager and challenger mindset with a passion for our brands and our consumers. We evaluate interns across two dimensions:

The "What" — Results
- Analytical rigor — synthesizes data and develops insight-driven, strategic recommendations

- Framing & storytelling — frames recommendations into a persuasive, clear narrativ e

- Consumer & shopper-driven insights —  demonstrates  genuine passion for understanding the consumer

- Strategic thought leadership — thinks critically, combines qualitative and quantitative inputs, and applies brand stewardship principle s

- Balanced priorities —  demonstrates  growing business acumen and proactively takes ownership

The "How" — Behaviors
- Cross-functional collaboration — actively engages beyond their immediate team

- Agility & navigating ambiguity — intellectually curious, quick-thinking, no ego

- Self-awareness & professional maturity — understands their impact and engages appropriately at all levels

- Receptive to coaching — takes feedback constructively and uses it to improve in real time

- Influence & drive for impact — results-oriented, evidence-based, with an enterprise mindset

- Relationship building — builds authentic connections across the organization

This role is specific to the Coffee Operating Unit of KDP. Following the successful acquisition of JDE Peet's in April 2026, the Coffee Operating Unit will become its own independent publicly traded company. For more information, please visit keurigdrpepper.com.

Senior Associate Brand Manager
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Job Overview:
At Keurig Dr Pepper, our mission is to provide a beverage for every need, everywhere people shop and consume. With a portfolio of 125+ iconic brands—including Dr Pepper®, Canada Dry®, Snapple®, Bai®, Mott’s®, CORE Hydration® and more—we are one of the largest food and beverage companies in the U.S. We put the consumer at the heart of everything we do, and our marketing team plays a critical role in delivering brand growth and long‑term category leadership.
We are seeking a Senior Associate Brand Manager (Sr. ABM) to accelerate the performance of one of our flagship brands. This role expands on the Associate Brand Manager position by taking on greater strategic responsibility, deeper cross‑functional leadership, and ownership of complex programs that drive brand and business results.
This role is based at the KDP headquarters in Frisco, Texas , with 10–15% travel and relocation required to the Greater Dallas area.

What You’ll Do
As a Senior Associate Brand Manager , you will be a high‑impact individual contributor responsible for leading major brand initiatives, informing long‑term strategy, and partnering across the organization to bring growth plans to life. You will demonstrate a general manager mindset, balancing strategic thinking with operational excellence.
In this role, you will:
Brand & Business Leadership
- Lead development of annual and multi‑year brand strategies using robust consumer insights, category trends, and competitive intelligence.
- Own business performance monitoring, diagnosing drivers across consumption, shipments, pricing, and media performance to inform leadership decisions.
- Translate brand strategy into actionable, integrated annual operating plans.

Marketing & Commercial Execution
- Lead major cross‑functional initiatives (innovation, communications, commercial programs, packaging updates, etc.) with limited supervision.
- Serve as the day‑to‑day lead with agency partners, elevating creative excellence, media effectiveness, and in‑market execution.
- Partner with shopper marketing, sales, and commercial teams to activate brand programs across key retail customers.

Insights & Analytics
- Leverage consumer research, syndicated data, KPI tracking, and financial modeling to build data‑backed recommendations.
- Proactively develop optimization plans based on ROI, media effectiveness, pricing performance, and competitive actions.

Budget & Investment Management
- Manage substantial brand budgets, ensuring disciplined allocation of resources to drive short‑ and long‑term growth.
- Present budget recommendations and trade‑off decisions to managers and cross‑functional leadership.

Leadership & Influence
- Mentor Associate Brand Managers and interns, supporting capability building across the broader marketing team.
- Influence cross‑functional partners—including Insights, R&D, Sales, Finance, Supply Chain—through clear storytelling and strong business cases.

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
The Senior Procurement Analyst – External Manufacturing supports the development, execution, and governance of procurement strategies for external manufacturing partners, including co‑manufacturers and repackers. The role provides analytical horsepower, financial insight, and decision support across sourcing, supplier performance, productivity, and risk management.

This position sits within Procurement and operates at the intersection of data, finance, and external manufacturing strategy, partnering closely with Sourcing Managers, Supply Chain, Planning, Finance, Quality, and Commercial teams. The role is designed for a high‑potential individual who can translate complex data into clear insights that enable better sourcing decisions and stronger supplier performance.

This position is a hybrid role based in Frisco, TX, with in-office work from Tuesday to Thursday and remote work on Monday and Friday.

Key Responsibilities
- Procurement Analytics & Decision Support - Develop and maintain analytical models to support sourcing strategies, make‑vs‑buy evaluations, and capacity decisions.
- Build scenarios comparing cost, service, risk, and productivity tradeoffs across external manufacturing options.
- Provide rapid, decision‑ready analysis to support live sourcing events, negotiations, and urgent business needs.
- Prepare fact‑based recommendations and executive‑ready materials to support sourcing and leadership decisions.

- Financial & Productivity Analysis - Support conversion cost modeling, total cost of ownership analyses, and margin impact assessments.
- Track productivity initiatives, savings delivery, and financial benefits in partnership with Finance and Sourcing Managers.
- Support AOP, forecast, and variance analysis related to external manufacturing spend and performance.

- Supplier Performance & Data Governance - Design, maintain, and automate supplier performance dashboards covering service, cost, quality, and risk metrics.
- Support Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) through data preparation, insights generation, and action tracking.
- Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and transparency across procurement and supply chain systems.

- Contract & Risk Analytics Support - Support contract lifecycle management through data analysis, benchmarking, and compliance tracking.
- Assist in supplier due diligence by analyzing financial health, capacity, operational resilience, and risk indicators.
- Partner with Procurement, Legal, and Supply Chain to strengthen risk visibility and governance discipline.

- Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Continuous Improvement - Act as a thought partner to Sourcing Managers by proactively identifying insights, risks, and improvement opportunities.
- Collaborate with Planning, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, and Commercial teams to align assumptions and data inputs.
- Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate procurement analytics and reporting

- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Finance, Business, Analytics, or a related field
- 4–7 years of experience in procurement, supply chain, finance, operations, or analytics roles (CPG/manufacturing preferred)
- Strong analytical and financial modeling skills with the ability to distill insights for senior stakeholders
- Experience supporting or working with manufacturing, external suppliers, or complex networks strongly preferred
- Advanced proficiency in Excel; experience with SAP, Power BI, or similar analytics tools preferred
- Strong communication skills with the ability to translate data into business implications
- Ability to operate effectively in a fast‑paced, matrixed organization

- Sourcing leaders are enabled by clear, trusted, decision‑ready analytics.

jobs.title: Director, Procurement & Category Management – Logistics & Warehousing
jobs.location: Burlington, Massachusetts, United States; Essex Junction, Vermont, United States; Montreal, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) maintains one of the most complex networks in North America. Freight market volatility, capacity swings, fuel and accessorial inflation, warehouse rate escalation, and an evolving distribution footprint make logistics one of the highest-impact, highest-visibility categories in the enterprise.

The Director of Procurement & Category Management – Logistics & Warehousing owns sourcing and category strategy for the full logistics services portfolio, including truckload, less-than-truckload, intermodal, dedicated fleet, parcel, ocean and air freight, drayage, final mile, and third-party warehousing and distribution services.

This leader moves the function towards strategic leadership and transformation. The role will challenge and reshape the logistics operating and supplier model: bringing procurement leadership to network strategy, 3PL architecture, control tower design, make/buy decisions, and other structural choices that influence cost, service, resiliency, and enterprise agility.

The role partners with Logistics Operations, Transportation Planning, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and Sustainability to translate requirements into operating strategies that support supply chain performance objectives.
Reporting to North America Procurement leadership, this position is hybrid and leads a team of procurement and category management professionals supporting the North America business. Some travel is required for supplier business reviews, network site visits, and bid negotiations.

The position is based in Burlington, MA, Montreal, Canada, or Essex, VT  office and will have a hybrid schedule.

Category scope: Truckload, LTL, intermodal, parcel and small package, ocean and air freight, drayage, final mile, freight brokerage and managed transportation, 3PL and contract warehousing, co-packing logistics, returnable assets and pallets, and transportation technology (TMS/WMS, visibility and freight audit & pay).

Essential Responsibilities
- Own end-to-end category strategy for logistics & warehousing spend, building multi-year roadmaps that balance total cost, service, capacity assurance, and risk.
- Lead annual and in-year bid events, and RFPs across modes; design lane-level award strategies, routing guide construction, and carrier allocation to maximize coverage and rate performance.
- Build should-cost, cost-to-serve, and index-based rate models; manage fuel surcharge programs, accessorial schedules, detention and demurrage exposure, and contractual escalation mechanisms.
- Negotiate master transportation, brokerage, dedicated fleet, and warehousing, SLAs, indemnity, insurance, and payment terms agreements in partnership with Legal and key stakeholders
- Source and manage 3PL and warehousing including, but not limited to: site selection support, storage and handling rate structures, labor assumptions. This is inclusive of start-up and exit provisions.
- Develop sourcing strategies in partnership with Logistics Operations and Network Planning that support network design, DC optimization and freight consolidation opportunities.
- Serve as the partner to North America Supply Chain, influencing decisions across network design, 3PL strategy, control tower capabilities, make/buy alternatives, capacity models, and governance.
- Lead logistics procurement transformation initiatives. Rethink how KDP buys, governs, and partners with transportation, warehousing, managed transportation, and technology providers.
- Leverage global JDE/KDP scale, supplier relationships, benchmarks, market intelligence, and cross-region synergies where they create value, while tailoring solutions to North America.
- Own market intelligence for freight and warehousing, using capacity, rate index, and macroeconomic data to forecast inflation and inform AOP.
- Mitigate risk across the provider base through capacity contingency planning, due diligence, safety and DOT/FMCSA compliance and business continuity planning.
- Establish carrier and provider KPIs and governance through scorecards, quarterly business reviews, continuous improvement programs, corrective action plans, and escalation protocols.
- Develop executive relationships with strategic transportation, warehousing, and logistics providers to drive innovation, capacity assurance, service improvements, and long-term value creation.
- Support supply chain service, resiliency, and performance objectives through best-in-class vendor management and sourcing strategies.
- Advance sustainability commitments within the category, including carrier emissions reporting, load optimization, and supplier diversity participation.
- Strengthen category capability through TMS, freight audit and pay, and analytics tools; improve data quality, spend visibility, and contract compliance across the provider base.
- Build and develop a high-performing team, fostering capability growth, engagement, accountability, and succession readiness.
- Champion collaboration across Procurement, Logistics, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, Customer Service, and Sustainability to ensure effective execution and sustainable results.

Key Performance Indicators
- Delivery of annual productivity, cost avoidance, and value creation against AOP.
- Total cost performance, including cost per case, cost per mile, cost per hundredweight, and warehousing cost per pallet position.
- Rate performance versus market indices and bid-award realization against contracted rates.
- Provider service performance: on-time in-full (OTIF), tender acceptance, primary carrier compliance, claims and damage rates.
- Control of accessorial, detention, demurrage, and spot market exposure.
- Capacity assurance, contract coverage, and routing guide depth across critical lanes
- Savings pipeline health, forecast accuracy, and realization of approved initiatives.
- Stakeholder satisfaction and business partner effectiveness.
- Team engagement, talent development, retention, and succession readiness.

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
As a North America Tax Compliance Manager, you will oversee the preparation, review, and filing of the Company's U.S. and Canadian tax compliance obligations, ensuring adherence to federal, state, provincial, and local tax regulations. This role requires strong technical tax expertise across both jurisdictions, project management skills, and the ability to collaborate across Finance, Accounting, Treasury, Legal, HR/Payroll, and external advisors to ensure accurate and timely compliance filings.

You will lead U.S. and Canadian income tax compliance processes, support tax audits and controversy matters, drive process improvements, leverage technology to increase efficiency, and provide leadership and development opportunities for tax team members. The position plays a critical role in maintaining the Company's North America tax compliance framework and supporting strategic tax initiatives.

This position is part of the Coffee Beverage Operating Unit of Keurig Dr Pepper and reports to the Sr. Director, Tax.
---
Position Responsibilities
- Lead the preparation, review, and filing of U.S. federal, state, and local income tax returns and Canadian federal and provincial income tax returns.
- Manage all aspects of North America tax compliance, including income tax returns, tax elections, information returns, and related filings.
- Coordinate tax compliance calendars and ensure all filing deadlines and payment obligations are met accurately and timely.
- Manage U.S. federal and state estimated tax payments and Canadian installment payment calculations and forecasts.
- Coordinate with internal stakeholders and external service providers to gather, validate, and analyze information required for tax filings.
- Review tax returns, workpapers, and supporting documentation to ensure technical accuracy and compliance with applicable tax laws and regulations.
-  Support tax audits, examinations, notices, inquiries, and controversy matters involving the IRS, CRA, and state and provincial taxing authorities.
- Monitor changes in U.S. and Canadian tax legislation and evaluate the impact on the Company's compliance obligations.
- Oversee preparation and review of tax compliance reporting packages for U.S. and Canadian legal entities.
- Collaborate with Tax Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, FP&A, Payroll, and Legal teams to ensure consistency between tax compliance, tax accounting, and financial reporting.
- Support U.S. and Canadian tax provision processes by providing compliance-related data, analyses, and return-to-provision support.
-  Assist with implementation and maintenance of tax technology solutions, including OneSource, Corptax, and data automation tools.
- Develop and maintain tax compliance processes, policies, and documentation to improve efficiency and strengthen internal controls.
-  Ensure SOX controls related to tax compliance are appropriately documented, executed, and tested.
- Identify opportunities for automation, standardization, and process improvement across North American tax compliance functions.
-  Support tax planning initiatives, legal entity restructuring projects, and business transactions by providing compliance-related analysis and tax data.
- Prepare reports, presentations, and tax summaries for senior management.
- Train, coach, and develop Tax Team members.
- Other projects and duties as assigned.

jobs.title: Premier·ère analyste financier·ère | Senior Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Aperçu du poste:
Ce poste est rattaché à l’Unité Opérationnelle Café
Premier·ère analyste financier·ère

Département : Finance
Statut : Permanent
Lieu : Montréal

Nous recherchons un·e premier·ère analyste financier·ère très motivé·e, qui sera responsable de jouer un rôle clé en tant que partenaire financier au sein de notre équipe des finances de la logistique. Ce poste joue un rôle essentiel pour fournir un leadership financier, des analyses pertinentes et un soutien stratégique afin d’optimiser l’affectation des ressources au sein du réseau logistique. La personne idéale est autonome, dotée d’un esprit analytique, curieuse et débrouillarde. Vous excellez dans un environnement collaboratif, êtes passionné·e par le souci du détail et adoptez une approche proactive pour résoudre les problèmes.

Principales responsabilités :

Responsabilités opérationnelles (70 %)

Ce sont les tâches essentielles et récurrentes qui permettent à l’entreprise de bien fonctionner.

- Gérer le processus de clôture de fin de mois pour les activités logistiques avec précision et dans le respect des délais.
- Préparer des analyses mensuelles des écarts par rapport au budget, aux prévisions et à l’exercice précédent; fournir des commentaires détaillés et des recommandations afin de faciliter l’élaboration des projections financières.
- Tenir à jour et améliorer les outils et processus de rapports financiers afin de renforcer la transparence et de faciliter la prise de décision (p. ex., rapports, prévisions, facturation des fournisseurs).
- Mettre à niveau, automatiser et améliorer les outils de rapports et d’analyse.
- Soutenir les évaluations de performance des sites en fournissant des analyses financières détaillées, notamment des informations par catégorie et par fournisseur.
- Soutenir les relations opérationnelles grâce à des systèmes performants de création de rapports, de prévisions, de résolution de problèmes et de gestion des processus financiers.
- Préparer des bulletins financiers pour communiquer les résultats de fin de mois à l’aide d’indicateurs opérationnels avancés.

Responsabilités stratégiques (20 %)

Ce volet est axé sur l’analyse à long terme et les projets à valeur ajoutée.

- Participer aux discussions financières menées dans le cadre des cycles de planification (plan de fonctionnement annuel/AOP, prévisions) concernant les finances de la logistique, en coordonnant les informations fournies par la direction des sites et en veillant à l’alignement avec les priorités stratégiques.
- Collaborer avec des équipes interfonctionnelles afin d’identifier les possibilités de réduction des coûts et d’amélioration de l’efficacité.
- Contribuer à la préparation des présentations destinées aux principales parties prenantes et aux hauts dirigeants en fournissant des analyses financières approfondies.

Responsabilités de leadership (10 %)

Bien qu’il ne s’agisse pas d’un poste de gestionnaire d’employés, cette personne dirigera des projets et sera un partenaire clé de l’entreprise.

- Agir en tant que personne-ressource principale des finances au sein des équipes logistiques et établir des relations solides et collaboratives, en fournissant des conseils financiers et un soutien à la prise de décision.
- Collaborer avec les Contrôleurs et les Comptes à payer afin de définir les meilleures pratiques (p. ex., pour la facturation des fournisseurs).
- Diriger des initiatives visant à renforcer les compétences financières au sein de l’équipe logistique grâce à des formations et à une communication régulière (p. ex., notions de base sur le compte de résultat/P&L, utilisation de l’outil de suivi).
- Apporter son soutien aux audits internes et externes, au besoin.

Qualifications professionnelles :
- Baccalauréat en : finances, comptabilité ou domaine connexe.
- Au moins 2 ans d’expérience, de préférence dans les analyses de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
- Capacité avérée à collaborer au sein d’une équipe et à travailler efficacement avec différents services de l’entreprise.
- Solides compétences analytiques et souci du détail.
- Maîtrise de Microsoft Excel; expérience des outils de visualisation de données (p. ex., Tableau, Power BI) et de SAP.
- Excellentes aptitudes à la communication écrite et orale.
- Attitude positive, curiosité pour trouver des réponses et ingéniosité pour résoudre les problèmes de manière autonome.
- Expérience en matière de processus de clôture mensuelle, de prévisions annuelles ou de rapports financiers.

Keurig Dr Pepper Canada est une importante société multinationale de boissons, avec des bureaux partout dans le monde et au Canada. D'un océan à l'autre, Keurig Dr Pepper Canada offre une boisson pour chacun et pour chaque occasion, et ce, pour tous les Canadiens. En raison de la portée mondiale et nationale du rôle pour lequel nous recrutons ci-dessus, ainsi que des besoins interfonctionnels requis pour ce rôle, nous avons déterminé que le français et l'anglais (écrit et parlé) sont requis. De plus, nous avons évalué que la connaissance de l'anglais déjà exigée des autres employés est insuffisante pour l'exécution des tâches nécessitant la connaissance de l'anglais et que le nombre de postes pour lesquels nous exigeons cette connaissance est le plus restreint possible pour assurer la réalisation efficace de notre mission.

Senior Financial Analyst

Department: Finance
Status: Permanent
Location: Montreal

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Financial Analyst to serve as a key finance business partner for our logistics finance team. This role is critical in providing financial leadership, insightful analysis, and strategic support to optimize resource allocation within the logistics network. The ideal candidate is autonomous, analytically driven, curious, and resourceful. You thrive in a collaborative environment and are passionate about digging into the details and develop a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Key Responsibilities:

Operational (70%)

These are the core, recurring tasks that keep the business running smoothly.

- Manage the month-end close process for the logistics business with accuracy and timeliness.
- Prepare monthly variance analyses vs. budget, forecast, and prior year; provide detailed commentary and recommendations to facilitate financial projections
- Maintain and improve financial reporting tools and processes to enhance transparency and decision-making (e.g., reporting, forecasting, vendor invoicing).
- Upgrades, automates and improves reporting and analytical tools.
- Support location performance reviews by providing detailed financial analysis, including categorical and vendor insights.
- Support operational relationships through robust reporting, forecasting, issue resolution, and financial process management.
- Prepare financial flashes to signal month-end performance using advanced operational signals.

Strategic (20%)

This component focuses on long-term analysis and value-add projects.

- Participate in financial discussions during planning cycles (Annual Operating Plan, Forecasts) for logistics finance, coordinating input from location leadership and ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify cost-saving opportunities and efficiency improvements.
- Contribute to the preparation of presentations for key stakeholders and senior leaders by providing meaningful financial insights.

Leadership (10%)

While not a people-management role, this person will lead projects and be a key partner to the business.

- Act as the primary finance contact person within the logistics teams and build strong & collaborative relationships, providing financial guidance and decision support.
- Collaborate with Controllership and Accounts Payable to establish best practices (e.g., vendor invoicing).
- Lead initiatives to enhance financial acumen within the logistics team through training and regular communication (e.g., P&L basics, tracker usage).
- Support internal and external audits as required.

Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in: Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
- 2+ years’ experience, prefer experience performing supply chain analysis
- Proven ability to work collaboratively in a team environment and partner effectively with various business functions.
- Strong analytical skills with meticulous attention to detail.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) and SAP.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- A can-do attitude, with the curiosity to seek out answers and the resourcefulness to solve problems independently.
- Experience with month-end processes, annual forecasting or financial reporting

Aperçu du poste:
Analyste Financier Principal – Analyses financières et planification (FP&A)
Ce poste est rattaché à l’Unité Opérationnelle Café

Département : Finance
Statut : Permanent
Lieu : Montréal

L’analyste financier principal FP&A joue un rôle clé dans le soutien des activités financières des Services de café Van Houtte. Ce poste est responsable de la gestion des finances opérationnels et administratifs incluant les résultats de fin de mois, les analyses d’écart, la budgétisation et les prévisions, tout en collaborant avec l’ensemble des départements pour assurer l’alignement budgétaire et une gestion efficace des coûts.

Ce poste relève du Premier Directeur Finance, Planification et Analyse financière.

Responsabilités

Stratégiques 30 %
- Agir en tant que partenaire d’affaire de confiance auprès des équipes des opérations de l’entreprises.
- Soutenir l’élaboration de plans financiers à long terme et des stratégies d’investissement pour l’entreprise.
- Moderniser, automatiser et améliorer les outils de rapports et d’analyses.
- Effectuer des analyses comparatives des coûts et des processus d’affaires, identifier les écarts et participer au développement de plans d’action pour adopter des pratiques exemplaires et soutenir les prévisions financières.
- Appuyer l’équipe de gestion dans différents projets spéciaux.
- Veiller à ce que l’entreprise respecte toutes les exigences réglementaires, ainsi que les politiques, les procédures et les normes éthiques établies par Keurig.

Opérationnelles 65 %
- Diriger le processus de production de rapports de fin de mois actuel ainsi que des prévisions budgétaires annuelles et trimestrielles avec exactitude et ponctualité.
- Responsable de la préparation de l’états financiers réel en fournissant les explications d’écarts détaillés entre les résultats réels, les prévisions et l’année précédente sur toute la section des coûts d’opération (effectifs, pièces, flotte automobiles, amortissements, coûts administratifs).
- Responsable de la préparation des documents de présentation des résultats réels et prévisionnels.
- Soutenir les initiatives et processus de productivité.
- Responsable du calcul des commissions périodique et des bonis annuels de l’équipe des ventes.
- Participer, en collaboration avec l’équipe comptable, au processus de décompte d’inventaire.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe des opérations afin de générer une forte performance opérationnelle et développer des outils qui aideront à en assurer le suivi.

Leadership 5 %
- Favoriser des relations de collaboration solides avec les équipes interfonctionnelles, en faisant preuve de leadership financier et de crédibilité.
- Maintenir les plus hauts standards d’intégrité et de confidentialité dans la gestion des données financières et RH sensibles.
- Être responsable de l’atteinte des objectifs annuels et des évaluations trimestrielles.
- Coordonner la mise à jour de la description de poste.
- Être responsable de l’autoévaluation annuelle de performance.

Qualifications requises
- Baccalauréat en finance ou en comptabilité, le titre CPA est un atout
- Minimum de 3 ans d’expérience pertinente en finance, budgétisation et prévision
- Connaissance générale des principes comptables et de contrôle des coûts
- Bilinguisme requis (français et anglais)

Compétences
- Approche hautement analytique, avec un fort désir de comprendre les moteurs de la performance.
- Autonomie, motivation et esprit entrepreneurial; capacité à résoudre les enjeux jusqu’à leur conclusion.
- Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale; à l’aise de communiquer avec la haute direction.
- Fort esprit d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes complexes, avec capacité à établir des relations de travail stratégiques.
- Capacité d’adaptation, gestion de plusieurs priorités et flexibilité à assumer des responsabilités supplémentaires.
- Compétences techniques et analytiques solides; capacité à relier les informations et à les traduire en actions concrètes.
- Capacité à modéliser des exigences d’affaires et à préparer des analyses de type « scénarios ».
- Autonomie dans la gestion de projets, de la conception à la mise en œuvre, avec peu de supervision.
- Compétences en planification et en prévision.
- Compétences en gestion de projet, approche logique de la résolution de problèmes, pensée analytique et compréhension globale avec focus tactique à court terme.
- Capacité à établir de solides relations avec l’équipe finance, les groupes fonctionnels, les pairs interfonctionnels et la haute direction.
- Capacité à respecter les normes de sécurité, à participer à l’amélioration continue sur le terrain et à suivre les meilleures pratiques manufacturières.
- Conformité aux politiques et procédures de KDP Canada ainsi qu’à sa mission et ses valeurs.
- Disponibilité à travailler selon un horaire flexible si requis.
- Connaissance des techniques d’amélioration des processus.
- Maîtrise avancée de MS Office (Word, Excel et PowerPoint).

CAD $78,300.00- $103,400.00 annually.

Location: Montreal

The role reports to the Senior Manager, FP&A.

Strategic 30%
- Act as a trusted business partner to the company’s operations teams.
- Support the development of long-term financial plans and investment strategies for the company.
- Modernize, automate, and improve reporting and analysis tools.
- Conduct benchmarking analyses of costs and business processes, identify variances, and participate in the development of action plans to adopt best practices and support financial forecasting.
- Support the management team with various special projects.
- Ensure that the company complies with all regulatory requirements, as well as the policies, procedures, and ethical standards established by Keurig.

Operational 65%
- Lead the current month-end reporting process, as well as the annual and quarterly budget forecasting processes, with accuracy and timeliness.
- Responsible for preparing actual financial statements by providing detailed variance explanations between actual results, forecasts, and the prior year for all operational cost categories, including headcount, parts, vehicle fleet, depreciation, and administrative costs.
- Responsible for preparing presentation materials for actual and forecasted results.
- Support productivity initiatives and processes.
- Responsible for calculating periodic commissions and annual bonuses for the sales team.
- Participate, in collaboration with the accounting team, in the inventory count process.
- Work closely with the operations team to drive strong operational performance and develop tools to help monitor it.

Leadership 5%
- Foster strong collaborative relationships with cross-functional teams, demonstrating financial leadership and credibility.
- Uphold the highest standards of integrity and confidentiality when dealing with sensitive financial and HR data.
- Responsible for completing yearly objectives and quarterly assessment.
- Coordinate efforts for keeping position description up to date.
- Responsible for completing yearly performance assessment.

Qualifications
- Bachelor degree in finance or accounting, CPA designation is an asset
- 3+ years of relevant experience in finance, budgeting and forecast
- General knowledge of accounting and cost control principles
- Bilingualism (French and English required)

Skills
- Highly analytical approach, constantly seeking to understand the driver for results.
- Self-managed, motivated, entrepreneurial style; brings matter to resolution.
- Excellent written and verbal communications skills; comfortable communicating with executive management.
- Strong drive for results and complex problems solving skills coupled with the ability to build solid strategic working relationships.
- Must be adaptable, able to multi-task and take on additional responsibilities as necessary.
- Strong analytical, technical skills and ability to link information together; capable of translating findings into business actions.
- Ability to model business requirements and prepare "what-if" analysis.
- Ability to take projects from the ground up to ending stage with minimal supervision.
- Planning and forecasting skills.
- Requires Project management skills, a logical approach to problem solving, analytical skills and a big-picture understanding with short term tactical focus.
- Ability to effectively build solid relationships with the finance team, functional group, cross-functional peers and upper level management.
- Ability to follow KDP Canada policies and procedures as well as uphold our purpose and values.

- Ability to work flexible hours as required.
- Familiarity with process improvement techniques.

- Advanced knowledge and proficiency of MS Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint).

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Are you ready to join a growing, dynamic company? Keurig Dr Pepper is a modern beverage company, with more than 125 brands people know and love. We challenge the usual and always push beyond the expected. We are building a culture that is our competitive advantage – one that is growth focused, change resilient, collaborative, innovative, nimble, diverse and inclusive.

Are you ready to do impactful work?  You’ll coach and mentor leaders. You’ll create and implement ambitious people strategies. You’ll play an important leadership role in our diversity & inclusion efforts. You’ll work collaboratively with business partners and Centers of Excellence to deliver solutions that propel the business forward.

Are you ready to grow? Here’s what will make you successful at KDP! We love passionate, courageous HR leaders who work with agility and are excited by new challenges. You’ll need consulting and influencing skills, a team-first, entrepreneurial spirit, business insight and analytical capability, and a heart for supporting the needs of our employees.

Will you be the next member of our talented team? If you’re ready, here’s more about the job!

This role supports our bottling facility in Ottumwa, IA. The Ottumwa site will require boots on the ground support involving supervisor trainings on contract, policies, and procedures as well as implementing digital processes to replace paper-based systems for efficiency.

As a Senior Human Resources Business Partner , you will leverage your business acumen to lead HR programs and processes for your site(s) and / or region(s). You will consult with leaders on all aspects of people leadership to ensure positive employee / labor relations, supporting the needs of the business while at the same time ensuring the fair and equitable treatment of our employees. You will lead small to medium size projects and will track project goals and tasks, report on progress, make recommendations and help with implementation. You will also ensure consistent and equitable application of organizational policies and procedures across a functional area or location and execute on talent initiatives. You will act as a change agent to enable the growth & development of our people and the organization/function.

Your Responsibilities will include:
- Coach and develop leaders in all areas of people leadership, including performance management and talent development, among others.
- Lead HR related projects and deployments and provide change management leadership where needed. Manage daily employee and labor relations and perform initial investigations of employee complaints and alleged policy violations, escalating where necessary.
- Partner with our COE teams to implement and monitor compliance with KDP policy, HR systems, and applicable federal/state law (including but not limited to 1-9s, personnel files, Worker’s Compensation, EEO, ADA, FMLA) and collective bargaining agreements.
- Partner with our Talent Acquisition team to track and report on open positions and help manage the position requisition process for internal transfers to ensure accuracy of postings and facilitate internal movement.
- Apply analytical skills to collect and synthesize data, formulate recommendations based on data trends and insights, and influence where needed to gain support for business proposals.
- Develop and / or deploy various communication materials (e.g., PowerPoint presentations, termination letters, and other employment-related correspondence).
- Travel may be required where your role includes the support of multiple locations.

Total Rewards:
- Salary Range: $72,100 - $118,800
- Actual placement within the compensation range may vary depending on experience, skills, and other factors
- Benefits, subject to election and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Paid Time Off (including paid parental leave, vacation, and sick time), 401k with company match, Tuition Reimbursement, and Mileage Reimbursement
- Annual bonus based on performance and eligibility

Requirements:
Education & Experience:
- Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, related field or professional experience equivalent; Master’s degree preferred
- A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in HR roles within fast-paced and matrix organizations
- Experience with collective bargaining, negotiations, and consultations with labor unions
- Advanced skills using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams)

Successful candidates will also demonstrate these additional qualifications:
- Proven ability to understand business goals and then design & implement new approaches, policies and procedures to affect continual improvements in business objectives, productivity and development of the HR function within the company
- Proven bias for action as evidenced through proactive, innovative and value-creating solution implementation
- Proven ability to navigate ambiguity within a complex, dynamic and rapidly changing business environment
- Proven ability to seamlessly transition between strategic thinking and tactical execution
- Proven ability to prioritize the most impactful work amidst multiple competing priorities
- Success in creating & driving effective and positive employee and labor relations for large populations of hourly employees in a distribution and / or manufacturing environment
- Success in leading and managing projects that require strong stakeholder management and alignment

Job Overview:
Senior Financial Analyst – Trade Finance

The Sr Financial Analyst – Trade Finance provides support to the Sales and Finance teams to ensure effective management of trade spend within budgets and ensuring compliance in the Trade Promotion Management (TPM) system. The Sr Financial Analyst supports and monitors the Sales Teams’ use of Demantra to ensure the most accurate trade spend estimates possible. The role will also be tasked with analysis of spend, identify optimization opportunities and collaborate with Finance leadership on total P&L management.

This role is aligned to the Coffee Operating Unit.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES: None

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Provide trade management guidance and training to Field Sales in the effective implementation of customer specific programs and national promotional programs for customers. Act as the “hub” for trade Spend tracking, planning and monitoring.
Provide ongoing Demantra trade promotion management system guidance to field sales to ensure promotional spend is accurately captured and system tasks are managed.
Conduct Demantra software and usage training with field sales as needed.
Lead the review and utilization of promotional spend reports with field sales to ensure accurate financial liability accrual.
Develop and maintain financial reports in Excel on key performance indicators
Ensure adequate financial control and policy adherence in the Demantra TPM arena with the Sales Team
Collaborate with IT, Finance, Revenue Growth Management, Accounting and Sales to administer the Demantra TPM system as efficiently and effectively as possible.
Calculate and validate customer rebate calculations as necessary for large customer rebate contracts.
Perform reconciliation of planned trade spend with actual spend as part of monthly close process.
Provide input & insight to overall monthly financial forecasting process

OTHER NECESSARY FUNCTIONS:
Models the Keurig Dr Pepper values
Follows all policies, procedures, ergonomic standards and safety requirements directed by Keurig Dr Pepper and the department
Performs other job related duties as requested by management

• It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

Requirements:

- Excellent reporting and data analysis skills in Excel
- Experience with utilizing forecast data, distributor data, syndicated data and sales shipment information.
- Experience with Trade Promotion Management systems (TPM -Demantra preferred) and TPO software preferred

- Ability to work flexible hours.

- Excellent communication skills, including written and presentation skills.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Corporate Finance, US Coffee (MBA)
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Summer 2027 Intern - Corporate Finance, US Coffee (MBA)

We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Finance MBA professional to support royalty forecasting, reporting, and partner brand financial management. This role will be responsible for interpreting complex licensing and royalty agreements, developing financial models to forecast and actualize royalty obligations, and providing actionable insights to support business planning and partner relationships.

The ideal candidate will combine strong financial modeling skills with the ability to translate contractual language into accurate financial outcomes. This position plays a critical role in ensuring royalty payments are calculated, forecasted, accrued, and paid accurately across a diverse portfolio of licensed and partner brands.

Schedule:
- The KDP Summer 2027 Intern Program runs from June 7th - August 13th, 2027
- Location: Burlington, MA
- Full-time; 40 hours per week
- Monday-Friday
- 8:00am until 5:00pm
- Hybrid, in-office 3 days a week

What you will do:
Financial Modeling & Forecasting
- Develop and maintain comprehensive royalty forecasting models that estimate quarterly and annual royalty expenses by partner brand.
- Create processes to compare forecasts against actual royalty expenses and identify key drivers of variances.
- Support budgeting, long-range planning, and monthly financial close activities related to royalty obligations.
- Recommend improvements to forecasting methodologies and reporting tools to enhance accuracy and efficiency.

Royalty Actualization & Reporting
- Calculate, validate, and reconcile royalty payments owed to partner brands based on sales activity and contractual agreements.
- Prepare quarterly royalty accruals and support payment processing activities.
- Analyze royalty trends, identify anomalies, and investigate discrepancies between forecasts and actual results.
- Generate regular reporting and executive-level insights regarding royalty obligations, partner brand performance, and financial impacts.

Variety Pack & Multi-Brand Royalty Analysis
- Analyze complex product portfolios, including variety packs containing multiple brands.
- Determine appropriate royalty allocation methodologies for products that include multiple brand partners.
- Unravel and validate multi-brand royalty structures to identify which partner brands are owed royalties and calculate payment amounts by quarter.
- Develop scalable tracking and reporting solutions that improve visibility into variety pack royalty obligations.
- Collaborate with Commercial and Supply Chain teams to understand product composition changes that may impact royalty calculations.

Total Rewards:
- $2,250 per week
- Paid bi-weekly
- $7,000 sign-on bonus, paid withing first 30 days of employment

Requirements:
- Education/Experience: - Currently enrolled in MBA program
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or Economics, or related field

- Technical and Other Skills: - Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office necessary, especially in Excel

- Required Competencies and aptitudes: - Self-motivated team player with strong ability to interact with others, work under pressure, and adhere to deadlines
- Very strong analytical and critical thinking skills with the ability to propose positive business solutions to complex problems
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment with focused attention to detail
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills with ability to work cross-functionally at a high level of customer service
- Comfortable working with high volumes of data and the ability to identify and summarize key messages
- Detailed and process improvement oriented
- Coachable, open to feedback, eager to grow into a well-rounded finance professional
- Ability to handle confidential financial information with discretion
- Ability to work flexible hours as required
- Ability to follow Keurig Dr Pepper policies and procedures, as well as our operating principles

Please Note : You must be work authorized in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future. The Company cannot offer employment to F-1 (student) visa holders who require sponsorship in the future or cannot work now on a full-time basis.

jobs.title: Relief Account Sales Manager
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Relief Sales Manager for Greater Fort Worth and Arlington, TX
Hiring Immediately
The Relief Sales Manager is responsible for up-selling and fulfillment/replenishment, focusing on execution and merchandising. This person will be accountable for retention and penetration of large format customers by geography and handling on-premise customers. Supporting Keurig Dr Pepper brands like 7UP, Snapple, Core, Bai and other fan favorites to retail stores within the assigned territory.

Shift and Schedule
- Full-time
- 6:00 am until work is finished
- 5 scheduled shifts per week
- Weekends required (days off fall during the week)
- Flexibility to work overtime as needed

Position Responsibilities
- Sell Keurig Dr Pepper brands to maximize growth, share growth, distribution, and to obtain specific volume objectives by providing a seamless experience to customers in the absence of an Account Manager.
- Contact key personnel in assigned accounts pre-selling products, promotions, displays, point-of sale material, beverage section revamps, and service requirements.
- Develop and implement beverage shelf re-allocations designed to maximize the sales of Keurig Dr Pepper brands.
- Participate in the installation of revamped beverage sections, displays and placement of point of sale material according to company merchandising standards.
- Stock and merchandise Keurig Dr Pepper brands in the allocated beverage section, including racks and secondary displays.
- Assist in the sale, placement, and changing of vendors in chain store accounts; check regularly for proper mechanical operation, cleanliness, selection and product availability.
- Maintain accurate sales records for all assigned accounts, including special reports on promotional activity, competitive sales and space allocations.
- Maintain adequate amounts of back stock in each account to ensure product availability for in-store stocking and merchandising.

Total Rewards:
- Pay starting at $24.76 per hour. The employee will move to a higher rate of $26.12 per hour in the quarter after their 6 month anniversary.
- Benefits, subject to eligibility, and collective bargaining agreements (where applicable): Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Paid Time Off (including vacation and sick time), 401k with company match, Tuition Reimbursement, and Mileage Reimbursement

- Ability to lift, push, and pull a minimum of 50 pounds repeatedly.
- Possession of a valid driver's license.
- Proof of vehicle insurance
- Access to a dependable and reliable vehicle.

jobs.title: Étudiant(e), Superviseur(e) Production COOP d'automne | Student, Operations Supervisor Fall Co-op
jobs.description:
Aperçu du poste:
Étudiant(e), Superviseur(e) Production COOP d'automne | Student, Operations Supervisor Fall Co-op

Étudiant(e), Superviseur(e) de Production
8300 19e Avenue, Montréal, QC H1Z 4J8

Appel à tous les étudiants passionnés et ambitieux ! Préparez-vous à propulser votre carrière grâce à un stage inoubliable chez Keurig Dr Pepper, une entreprise qui allie innovation, saveur et enthousiasme à chaque gorgée. En tant que stagiaire enthousiaste, vous aurez l'occasion d'apprendre auprès de mentors expérimentés, de participer à des activités de développement professionnel et d'avoir un impact significatif sur notre entreprise   !

Nous avons cinq stages disponibles, un pour chaque quart de travail , en plus d’un poste flottant (voir ci-dessous).
- 4X10Jour - du lundi au jeudi de 6h30 AM à 17h00 PM
- 4X10Soir - du lundi au jeudi de 17h00 PM à 3h30 AM
- 3x12Jour - du vendredi au dimanche de 6h30 AM à 18h30 PM
- 3x12Nuit  - du vendredi au dimanche de 18h30 PM à 6h30 AM
- Flottant – Flexible pour se déplacer sur les 4 quarts de travail

Dans le cas des 5 postes disponibles, une certaine flexibilité sera demandée aux candidats sélectionnés.

Ton rôle:
En tant qu’ étudiant(e) en supervision de production , tu travailleras en étroite collaboration avec les superviseurs et les équipes de production afin de te familiariser avec les différentes facettes de la gestion des opérations manufacturières.
Tu contribueras aux activités quotidiennes de production, au suivi de certains indicateurs de performance ainsi qu’à des initiatives d’amélioration continue. Cette expérience te permettra de développer tes compétences en leadership, en résolution de problèmes et en gestion des opérations dans un environnement dynamique.

Tes responsabilités:
- Soutenir les superviseurs dans la coordination des activités quotidiennes de production.
- Participer au suivi des horaires et des priorités de production.
- Faire le suivi de certains indicateurs de production et aider à identifier les écarts ou les possibilités d’amélioration.
- Participer à des projets d’amélioration continue touchant notamment la sécurité, la qualité, l’efficacité et la réduction des pertes.
- Collaborer avec les employés de production et les différentes équipes afin de soutenir le bon déroulement des opérations.
- Contribuer à la mise à jour de procédures, d’outils de travail, de documents de formation et d’autres documents opérationnels.
- Participer à l’analyse de problématiques opérationnelles et proposer des pistes de solution avec l’accompagnement de l’équipe.
- Soutenir les initiatives visant à maintenir un environnement de travail sécuritaire, propre et conforme aux bonnes pratiques de fabrication (BPF).
- Collaborer avec différentes fonctions, notamment les équipes de qualité, d’ingénierie et des opérations, dans le cadre de projets ou d’initiatives.
- Préparer ou mettre à jour certains rapports et suivis liés aux activités de production.
- Développer une compréhension concrète du rôle d’un superviseur et des réalités liées à la gestion d’une équipe en milieu manufacturier.
- Signaler rapidement à son superviseur toute situation pouvant avoir un impact sur la sécurité ou la qualité des produits.

Qualifications professionnelles:
- Baccalauréat en ingénierie, en exploitation, en administration ou dans un domaine similaire (en cours ou terminé)
- Disponible à temps plein (40 heures par semaine) pour la saison estivale (début mai à fin août)
- Légalement autorisé à travailler au Canada
- Bilingue, FR & AN

Compétences:
- Compétences avérées en matière de leadership et de sollicitude envers les subordonnés, excellent esprit d’analyse et capacité à proposer des solutions à des problèmes.
- Aptitudes supérieures en communication et en organisation.
- Sens des priorités afin de satisfaire aux exigences de l’entreprise dans une perspective plus vaste.
- Capacité à travailler de façon autonome et en équipe dans un milieu en changement constant où les activités se déroulent à un rythme rapide, tout en faisant preuve de souci du détail.
- Capacité à tisser des relations constructives et efficaces par la diplomatie et le tact, de même que par le traitement équitable des employés.

Le titulaire fera partie d’une équipe dynamique et passionnée travaillant au service d’une entreprise en constante évolution.

Keurig Dr Pepper Canada est une importante société multinationale de boissons, avec des bureaux partout dans le monde et au Canada. D'un océan à l'autre, Keurig Dr Pepper Canada offre une boisson pour chacun et pour chaque occasion, et ce, pour tous les Canadiens. En raison de la portée mondiale et nationale du rôle pour lequel nous recrutons ci-dessus, ainsi que des besoins interfonctionnels requis pour ce rôle, nous avons déterminé que le français et l'anglais (écrit et parlé) sont requis. De plus, nous avons évalué que la connaissance de l'anglais déjà exigée des autres employés est insuffisante pour l'exécution des tâches nécessitant la connaissance de l'anglais et que le nombre de postes pour lesquels nous exigeons cette connaissance est le plus restreint possible pour assurer la réalisation efficace de notre mission.

* Le générique masculin est utilisé sans aucune discrimination et uniquement dans le but d'alléger le texte

Rémunération globale:
CAD $33.40 per hour

CAD $33.40 par heure

Exigences:
Student, Production Supervisor
8300 19th Avenue, Montréal, QC H1Z 4J8

Calling all passionate and ambitious students! Get ready to launch your career with an unforgettable internship at Keurig Dr Pepper, a company that combines innovation, flavor, and excitement in every sip. As an enthusiastic intern, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced mentors, participate in professional development activities, and make a meaningful impact on our business!

We have five internships available, one for each shift , plus one floating position (see below).
- 4x10 Day - Monday through Thursday, 6:30 AM to 5:00 PM
- 4x10 Evening - Monday through Thursday, 5:00 PM to 3:30 AM

jobs.title: Operations Supervisor
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
This role is aligned to the Coffee Operating Unit

Location: Spartanburg 2 – 3220 Moore Duncan Hwy, Suite 100, Gate A, Moore, SC 29369

Shift & Schedule
Initial Phase (First 6–8 Weeks):
- 1st Shift: Monday–Thursday, 6:30 AM–5:00 PM

Transition Phase (After 6–8 Weeks):
- Evening shift coverage may be required, Monday–Friday, 3:00 PM–11:30 PM.

Final/Eventually Permanent Phase (N1 Shift):
- Sunday–Tuesday, 6:30 PM–7:00 AM, with alternating Saturdays.

Alternative Night Shift Schedule:
- Weekend Night Shift: Friday–Sunday, 6:30 PM–7:00 AM (12-hour shifts)
or

- Monday–Friday Night Shift: 9:30 PM–6:00 AM (8-hour shifts)

As an Operations Supervisor , you will lead and develop a team of approximately 25 manufacturing associates in a highly automated, TPM-based production environment. You will foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement while partnering cross-functionally to optimize production efficiency, reduce costs, and deliver exceptional operational performance.
This role is ideal for a hands-on leader who enjoys coaching teams, solving problems, driving process improvements, and achieving results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Responsibilities
- Lead a team of approximately 25 operations associates through hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, development, and recognition.

- Drive best-in-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity metrics.

- Promote a culture focused on achieving zero injuries through safety observations, audits, training, and regulatory compliance.

- Ensure consistent product quality by leading right-first-time execution, layered process audits, and root cause corrective actions.

- Partner with Maintenance, Quality, Materials, and Distribution teams to maximize equipment uptime through TPM and preventive maintenance practices.

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
This is a 12 - Month contract position based in Newbridge, Co Kildare.

The Manager, Procurement Strategy and Capabilities is responsible for leading supplier onboarding and business transformation for the KDP Global Sourcing Ireland Buy-Sell operating model, with SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration (SCC), system testing, development cycle management and go-live readiness as the top priorities. The role supports delivery across process improvement, system enhancement, governance, reporting and digital transformation in partnership with Procurement, Finance, Legal, Tax, Supply Chain, Manufacturing and IT.

Working through cross-functional teams, the Manager coordinates onboarding activities, tracks actions and risks, supports issue resolution, and helps improve related processes and reporting. The role is project-specific to Ireland Buy-Sell, with additional associated tasks across Procurement Strategy and Capabilities as required .
Key Responsibilities
Supplier Onboarding
- Lead supplier onboarding and business transformation activities for the Ireland Buy-Sell model, with SAP Ariba SCC enablement as the top delivery priority.
- Coordinate end-to-end onboarding across suppliers, Category Managers, manufacturing sites, Finance, Legal, Tax, Supply Chain and IT.
- Manage system testing, user acceptance testing, defect tracking, cutover planning, go-live execution and hypercare activity.
- Drive development cycle management for required process and system enhancements, including requirements gathering, prioritisation , release planning, testing and deployment readiness.
- Maintain clear project plans, issue logs, risk trackers, status updates and governance materials to support delivery visibility and stakeholder alignment.

SAP Ariba SCC, SAP MM and Operational Support
- Use SAP Ariba SCC, SAP MM and related procurement systems to support supplier onboarding, operational execution and ongoing business process stability.
- Troubleshoot system and operational issues across SAP Ariba SCC, SAP MM, supplier transactions, purchase orders, confirmations, ASNs, GRNs and related process flows.
- Work with suppliers, manufacturing sites, Procurement, Finance and IT to investigate issues, agree resolutions and support timely closure of defects or process gaps.
- Identify recurring issues and drive continuous improvement opportunities to strengthen system performance, process compliance, supplier adoption and operational efficiency.

Reporting
- Provide clear visibility of onboarding status, milestones, delivery progress, risks, issues, dependencies and mitigation actions.
- Prepare stakeholder updates, governance materials, status reports and risk summaries to support timely decision-making.
- Maintain consistent templates, trackers and governance practices for onboarding, reporting, controls and compliance activities.
- Support audit requirements, operational controls and delivery in line with company policies, control standards and compliance requirements.

Business & Digital Transformation, Automation and AI
- S upport Procurement and IT Project Teams to implement Tools/Solutions included in our functional roadmap for 2027 .
- Identify and drive opportunities to simplify and automate project and procurement processes using Microsoft Copilot, Power BI, analytics and other digital or AI-enabled solutions.
- Use AI and data insights to strengthen planning, status reporting, risk identification and decision-making.
- Support the development of automated dashboards and self-service reporting capabilities.

Stakeholder Management
- Build effective relationships across Procurement, Finance, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, IT and external suppliers.
- Influence stakeholders and create alignment across functions without direct reporting authority.
- Facilitate workshops, governance reviews, testing sessions and project meetings.
- Communicate complex project information clearly to both operational and senior leadership audiences.

Total Rewards:
At KDP Ireland, you will find that:
- We aspire to have the top talent within the industry and are committed to maintaining an extraordinarily brilliant, remarkably diverse, and decidedly engaged team.
- We invest in the development and growth of our employees and promote continuous learning to enable progressive career tracks.
- We offer a competitive salary and bonus structure, and excellent employee benefits including private medical care, pension contributions, and holiday entitlements.
- We provide Global exposure – As a multi-national CPG with HQ offices in the USA and peers operating in five countries, there are opportunities travel to different countries and share international perspectives and experiences.
- We have an active interest in the community - We run events throughout the year to support local charities, people & communities.

Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in Business , Supply Chain, Procurement, Information Systems or a related discipline.
- Experience using SAP M aterials Management ideally in a Procurement environment .
- Project management qualification such as PMP, PRINCE2, Agile, Scrum or equivalent practical project delivery certification.
- 7+ years of experience in procurement operations, supply chain , supplier onboarding, business transformation or related project delivery .
- Proven experience coordinating cross-functional activities in a global or matrixed environment.
- Strong stakeholder management, communication, and facilitation skills.

Tools and Capabilities
- Proficiency with planning, tracking and collaboration tools such as Microsoft Planner, Excel, SharePoint, Teams, Smartsheet or Jira.
- Strong capability in action tracking, reporting, issue management, governance support and benefits tracking.
- Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills, with experience producing clear stakeholder-ready reporting.
- Use of Power BI, Microsoft Copilot and AI-enabled tools preferred
- Experience with  SAP Ariba SCC and procurement technology preferred.

Preferred Qualifications
- Project Management Professional (PMP) or PRINCE2 Practitioner certification / Agile, Scrum certification.
- SAP or SAP Ariba certification.

jobs.title: HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Are you ready to join a growing, dynamic company? Keurig Dr Pepper is a modern beverage company, with more than 150 brands people know and love. We challenge the usual and always push beyond the expected. We are building a culture that is our competitive advantage – one that is growth focused, change resilient, collaborative, innovative, nimble, diverse and inclusive.

Are you ready to do impactful work?   You’ll coach and mentor leaders. You’ll create and implement ambitious people strategies. You’ll play an important leadership role in our diversity & inclusion efforts. You’ll work collaboratively with business partners and Centers of Excellence to deliver solutions that propel the business forward.

Are you ready to grow?  Here’s what will make you successful at KDP! We love passionate, courageous HR leaders who work with agility and are excited by new challenges. You’ll need consulting and influencing skills, a team-first, entrepreneurial spirit, business insight and analytical capability, and a heart for supporting the needs of our employees.

Will you be the next member of our talented team?  If you’re ready, here’s more about the job!

Location: This role may be based out of our Pewaukee, WI facility and will require regular travel to our facilities in Tomah, Racine, and Oshkosh.

As a Human Resources Business Partner , you will work with managers and employees to address issues and concerns where judgment is required. You will interpret and enforce company policies and provide coaching to managers on all aspects of leadership and employee/labor relations.  You will help to define the organization's talent needs, including organization structure and staffing. As a key culture leader in the organization, you will also counsel employees on work-related challenges and provide guidance to managers with respect to implementing Human Resources programs for a function or location. You will also act as a change agent to enable the growth & development of our people and the organization/function.

Your Responsibilities will include:

- Coach and develop business partners in the areas of performance management and talent development, among others
- Assist with the development and facilitation of various training initiatives predicated on business needs and corporate goals
- Manage daily employee and labor relations and perform initial investigations of employee complaints and alleged policy violations, escalating where necessary
- Partner with HR Compliance Team to implement and monitor HR compliance with KDP policy, HR systems, and applicable federal/state law (including but not limited to 1-9s, personnel files, Worker’s Compensation, EEO, ADA, FMLA) and collective bargaining agreements
- Partner with our Talent Acquisition team to track and report on open positions and help manage the position requisition process for internal transfers to ensure accuracy of postings and facilitate internal movement
- Research and respond to initial unemployment requests for data as well as scheduling and notifying participants of upcoming hearings
- Apply analytical skills to collect and synthesize data, tell the story and formulate recommendations based on data trends and insights
- Develop basic communication materials (e.g., PowerPoint presentations, termination letters, and other employment-related correspondence)
- Travel required

Total Rewards:
- Salary range $62,500 - $95,000
- Actual placement within the compensation range may vary depending on experience, skills, and other factors
- Benefits, subject to election and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Paid Time Off (including paid parental leave, vacation, and sick time), 401k with company match, Tuition Reimbursement, and Mileage Reimbursement
- Annual bonus based on performance and eligibility

Requirements:
Education & Experience:
- Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, related field or professional experience equivalent
- A minimum of 4-6 years of progressive experience in HR roles within fast-paced and matrix organizations
- Experience with collective bargaining, negotiations, and consultations with labor unions
- Advanced skills using Microsoft Office Suite (Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams)

Successful candidates will also demonstrate these additional qualifications:
- Proven ability to understand business goals and then design & implement new approaches, policies and procedures to affect continual improvements in business objectives, productivity and development of the HR function within the company
- Proven bias for action as evidenced through proactive, innovative and value-creating solution implementation
- Proven ability to navigate ambiguity within a complex, dynamic and rapidly changing business environment
- Proven ability to seamlessly transition between strategic thinking and tactical execution
- Proven ability to prioritize the most impactful work amidst multiple competing priorities
- Success in creating & driving effective and positive employee and labor relations for large populations of hourly employees in a distribution and / or manufacturing environment
- Success in leading and managing projects, some of which may be large-scale, cross-functional, and require strong stakeholder management and alignment

Our offer:
